newsitem.title: USA: Mercedes US unit to get American CEO in '98.
newsitem.headline: Mercedes US unit to get American CEO in '98.

text.p: Mercedes-Benz of North America Inc Monday announced a major management succession plan that will put an American in charge of the company for the first time at the end of 1998.

The U.S. distribution arm of German luxury car maker Mercedes-Benz AG said its president and chief executive officer, Michael Bassermann, 61, will retire at the end of 1998. He will be succeeded by Michael Jackson, 48, a former mechanic who is now executive vice president of marketing, service and sales.
The transition comes at a time when Mercedes is launching a ambitious array of new products, including its new U.S-built M-Class sport/utility vehicle, the SLK roadster and CLK coupe.

"We have embarked on an unparalleled product offensive and have established very ambitious sales targets from now through the end of the decade," Bassermann said in a statement. "For this reason we have engineered an effective and efficient succession plan to maintain leadership continuity and, thus, our marketing momentum."
Bassermann, who began his automotive career in 1965 with Mercedes' parent company, Daimler-Benz AG, assumed leadership of Mercedes-Benz North America in 1992.
During his tenure, Mercedes' annual U.S. sales volume increased from 63,312 in 1992 to 90,844 in 1996.
